messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: citations for markdown
parts:
Hi list,

Like many on this list, I've starting to increasingly using markdown as my standard format.  I thought it would be nice to add citations the way I can with latex (using a bibtex file) or on wordpress (using a doi, without having to create the bibtex file), without having to run an extra converter.  I wrote a few little functions to do this, thought I'd share in case anyone finds them useful or has feedback on how to make this better: https://github.com/cboettig/knitcitations/blob/master/inst/examples/citations.md

basically uses inline R code to generate an inline citation, and stores the data on which papers are cited to generate a reference list at the end. 

Cheers,
-Carl



--
Carl Boettiger
UC Davis
http://www.carlboettiger.info/

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] citations for markdown
parts:
Dynamic generation of citations is a very good idea, and can be
generalized to other document formats as well. Originally I was mainly
thinking of citing R packages: we first record the package names, and
write a bib file later for all the packages used.

Regards,
Yihui
